newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Chirac to visit Argentina in March - French minister.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to visit Argentina in March - French minister.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will pay an official visit to Argentina next March to cement "excellent diplomatic and economic relations", French Trade Minister Yves Galland said Friday.
"Chirac will be here on an official visit in March 1997," he told a news conference. The planned trip follows a visit to France by Argentine President Carlos Menem in February.
Galland, who is in Buenos Aires heading a delegation of 50 business leaders seeking trade opportunities, said France has confidence in Argentina's economy.

"This confidence in Argentina was reinforced by the strength of its economy, which weathered the effect of the Mexican crisis and is now growing again," he said in reference to the devaluation of the Mexican peso which last year jolted emerging markets throughout the world.

France has invested some $5.0 billion in Argentina since Menem launched an ambitious privatization drive six years ago and Galland wants to interest French business in sell-offs still to come of Argentine ports, bridges and energy firms.
He promised France and Argentina would create structures to promote bilateral trade, commercial joint ventures and technology exchanges between small and medium companies.
Galland added a caution that Menem's Peronist government should guarantee the legal transparency of privatizations and concessions of public assets to insure the continuity of the investment process.
"I spoke of problems of legality with Menem and Argentine deputies and senators," he said.
Two French firms, Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) and construction firm Bouygues, have complained of legal problems in Argentine privatizations.
